tickets.title: A settled job's card shows its outcome
tickets.what:
when a HUD job settles, the Decision API reads the first lines of its report and its final status
and classifies the outcome: done / partial / failed / blocked, with a confidence. Home cards, the Inspector and the
progress board's slice block show it as a mark (e.g. a job whose report says live validation was not run shows
"partial"). This ticket also builds the shared path every later ticket uses: decision calls for display labels go to
Gemini first (free tier; the owner's key), fail over to OpenAI, are cached by input revision, and share an hourly cap.
They do not follow the Settings "Decision API" row (that row is Jev's browser jobs). Display only: a label never
changes a job's state or steers a worker.

Legacy Blocked by: None (GEMINI-DECIDE landed fe3aed6c)

acceptance.text: One decision call per settlement, input bounded to the report's head and the status; reopening the panel or an unchanged report makes no call
Outcome mark on Home, in the Inspector and on the progress board, EN and ZH, 80 and 120 columns
Master switch off or no decision key: no mark, no call
Gemini 429 falls over to OpenAI; the hourly cap holds; tests with a fake decision endpoint

tickets.title: Each job is labelled with its kind
tickets.what:
each HUD job gets a kind from its brief's title and goal: ui, bug fix, feature, refactor, review,
research, docs, chore (a job may carry more than one). The Inspector shows the kind. Settled jobs of the last 30 days
that have no label yet get one in the background, inside the shared hourly cap, newest first.

acceptance.text: One call per job, input bounded to the brief's title and goal; cached, so a job is labelled once
Inspector shows the kind, EN and ZH
Background backfill of the last 30 days, newest first, never above the hourly cap

tickets.title: The Project tab shows which model fits which kind of work
tickets.what:
a "Model fit" section on the Project tab: for each job kind, each role · model · thinking that ran
it, with the number of runs, the outcome split (done / partial / failed / blocked) and the median duration. Read only
from the labels of 01 and 02 and the jobs' own records; no model call of its own.

acceptance.text: Section on the Project tab with kinds as groups and one row per role · model · thinking
Counts and median duration match the labelled jobs in a synthetic fixture
Unlabelled jobs are counted as "unlabelled", not dropped
EN and ZH, 80 and 120 columns

tickets.title: A running job that is going in circles is marked
tickets.what:
for a running card (a HUD job or a native subagent) that has been quiet for a few minutes, the
Decision API reads its recent public activity (the last dozen tool calls and their result summaries, already read for
its sentence) and judges whether it is progressing or repeating the same failure. A "looping" verdict shows a ⚠ on the
card with the confidence in the Inspector. At most one call per card per 5 minutes, only while it stays quiet.
Display only: nothing is sent to the worker.

acceptance.text: No call for a card that has new activity or was judged less than 5 minutes ago
A synthetic session repeating one failing command is marked; a progressing one is not
The mark clears when new, different activity arrives
EN and ZH, 80 and 120 columns

tickets.title: Worker questions are sorted by what they need from the owner
tickets.what:
each question a worker asks is classified as design trade-off / clarification / needs the owner's
authorisation / blocked. The panel shows the category on the question and on its "decided for you" row; questions
that need the owner's authorisation are listed first. Display only: the category never answers or delays a question.

acceptance.text: One call per question, input bounded to the question file; cached by its revision
Category chip on pending questions and decided rows; authorisation questions sort first
EN and ZH, 80 and 120 columns

tickets.title: Review findings are counted by severity
tickets.what:
a review report's findings are classified as must fix / should fix / optional, whatever headings
the reviewer used. The progress board's slice block and the Inspector show the counts (e.g. "2 must fix · 3 should").
One call per review revision.

acceptance.text: Findings are split from the review's list items, bounded in count and length; one call per review revision
Counts on the progress board and in the Inspector; a review with no findings shows none
EN and ZH, 80 and 120 columns
